title: metadata-04: /changes updatedProperties and ignore rules
description:
draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-04 changes the /changes rules for ignoreMetadataOnlyChanges and updatedProperties.

-04 §3.3 ignoreMetadataOnlyChanges: "If the server cannot determine that an id's changes are metadata-only, it MUST include the id. Excluded ids do not count toward maxChanges. ... When this argument is true, updatedProperties (defined below) MUST NOT list metadata or privateMetadata. For Mailbox/changes it may list the count properties (Section 2.2 of [RFC8621]); for other types it MUST be null."
-04 §3.3 updatedProperties: "It is always present, and is null when updated is empty." "For Mailbox/changes, when every id in updated changed only in its counts (as defined there) and/or in metadata or privateMetadata, the value is the union of the count property names and the metadata property names that may have changed."
-04 §3 (new): "For other requests [whose using lacks urn:ietf:params:jmap:metadata] ... Foo/changes MUST behave as if ignoreMetadataOnlyChanges were true."
(-02: with the flag true, updatedProperties "MUST be null"; it did not say "always present".)

Affected:
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/changes.rs:1-18 module doc and :44-56 usage note: describe the -04 rules (maxChanges exclusion; uncertain ids included; Mailbox count+metadata union; implicit flag when the capability is not in using).
- crate-jmap-metadata-client/src/lib.rs:102-154 doc for IGNORE_METADATA_ONLY_CHANGES / is_metadata_only_change. With Mailbox/changes now able to return e.g. ["totalEmails","metadata"], is_metadata_only_change correctly returns false. Document that callers who want "only metadata plus counts changed" must handle that case themselves. Its section cites (§2.4/§2.5) are wrong even for -02 (/changes is §3.3).
- crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:153-154 ChangesResponse.updated_properties is skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none". -04 says the argument "is always present" (null when not a list) for listed types, so a server serializing through ChangesResponse cannot emit the required explicit null. Decide whether to always serialize it or leave that to metadata-aware servers. Changing it touches the tests at methods.rs:589-606 and :966, which assert omission; that is a contract change and needs a decision before touching those tests. Decoding is unaffected (default None).
notes: DECIDED by Mark 2026-10-20: emit updatedProperties (null or list) on every /changes response only when the request's using includes the metadata capability; otherwise keep RFC 8620 behaviour (omitted unless set). Existing omission tests at jmap-types methods.rs:589-606 stay valid for the no-capability case; add tests for the capability case quoting -04 §3.3.
